identity.title: Discovery of a Molecular Collision Front in Interacting Galaxies NGC 4567/4568 with ALMA

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present results of $^{12}$CO(*J* = 1–0) imaging observations of , a galaxy pair in a close encounter, with Atacama Large Millimetre/submillimetre Array.

evidence.quote: The pair is one of the ideal interacting galaxies for this purpose because of their alignment, vicinity (16 Mpc)

question.value: Is there a molecular collision front in the overlapping region of the early-stage interacting pair NGC 4567/4568, and what are the properties of the molecular gas and clouds there?

evidence.quote: molecular gas observation of interacting galaxies at the early stage is crucial because they should maintain conditions before or at the beginning of active star formation
CO observations towards the NGC 4567/4568 galaxy pair were carried out as an ALMA Cycle 1 program (2012.1.00759.S).
We present results of $^{12}$CO(*J* = 1–0) imaging observations
The 12-m array observations were performed using 36 antennas with C32-4 configuration.
Observations with Atacama Compact Array (ACA), which consists of ten 7-m antennas and two 12-m antennas for Cycle 1 observation, were also requested
The 12-m array observations were performed using 36 antennas with C32-4 configuration.
The combined cube has an angular resolution of 2$\ensuremath{''}$0 $\times$ 2$\ensuremath{''}$0 (equivalent to 155 pc $\times$ 155 pc at 16 Mpc)
our ALMA data cannot detect emission from extended structures larger than $\sim$20$^{\prime\prime}$ (corresponding to 1.55 kpc at 16 Mpc)
Resultant rms noise is 8.5 mJy beam$^{-1}$.
Total observed time on the source was 25.4 minutes, and 39 fields of view were required to cover whole region of the galaxy pair.
The total on-source time for the ACA 7-m array observations as 20.9 minutes.

results_numeric.quantity: Mean virial parameter of all clouds

evidence.quote: averaged $\alpha_{\mathrm{vir}}$ for all molecular clouds in NGC 4567/4568 is 0.27
a total of 215 clouds are resolved from the cube data, and four of them are found in the filamentary structure.

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular gas of the two galaxies connects smoothly in velocity across the overlap region, taken as evidence of a collision front; the filament coincides with an R-band dark lane.

evidence.quote: This molecular gas having large velocity width is direct evidence of a molecular collision front, which has never been observed.

claims.hypothesis: A molecular collision front exists in the overlap region
claims.experiment: PVD across the overlap region from the combined ALMA cube
claims.result: Gas connects smoothly with ~50 km/s velocity width
claims.finding: Direct evidence of a molecular collision front

evidence.quote: molecular gas in NGC 4567 and NGC 4568 smoothly connects with velocity width of approximately 50 km s$^{-1}$

claims.hypothesis: Clouds in the filament are gravitationally bound
claims.finding: Four clouds are bound, though the filament as a whole is unbound by m_vir/l

evidence.quote: almost all clouds (206/215) are gravitationally bound ($\alpha_{\mathrm{vir}}<1$), including the four gas clouds in the filament.

claims.hypothesis: The filament is consistent with shock-induced giant filament simulations
claims.experiment: Comparison of aspect ratio and properties with Saitoh09
claims.result: Aspect ratio 5 matches; mass two orders smaller
claims.finding: Filament likely shock-induced, possible super star cluster progenitor

evidence.quote: Although the mass of the filament we found is two orders of magnitude smaller than that of the numerical simulation, an aspect ratio of their long filamentary gas structure is 5

limitations_admitted.value: No total power data; about half of the CO flux is missing, so filament size and mass are lower limits.

evidence.quote: Note that the size and mass of the filament are a lower limit since about half of CO flux is missing as we described above.

referee_caveats_inferred: Virial analysis with half the flux missing may bias masses and alpha_vir
Velocity dispersion of 16.8 km/s from a 5 km/s channel cube; low alpha_vir may reflect the CO conversion factor
Filament virial result (unbound) vs clouds bound is not fully reconciled
Collision-front interpretation could be chance alignment with projection effects
